  "title": "Tesla, Inc. TSLA and SPCX Form Committees to Evaluate Potential Merger",
  "type": "equity_research",
  "priority": "high",
  "published": "2026-10-27",
  "insights": [
   "Musk said on the SpaceX Q3/26 earnings call that both SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees of independent directors to evaluate a merger at shareholders' request. Musk is a conflicted party and cannot take part in the committee discussions.",
   "Musk pushed back on the idea that a merger is certain, while personally supporting it. He said the committees have not agreed on terms and there is no guarantee they will.",
   "A transaction would need a 50% vote of all Tesla shares outstanding, not just those voting. Musk called this 'quite a high hurdle'.",
   "Musk cited synergies in superintelligence software, chip design, Terafab, robotics and connectivity.",
   "RBC thinks SPCX may need to pay a meaningful premium for TSLA shares. Musk controls about 20% of Tesla's voting power versus about 82% at SpaceX, which creates an asymmetric governance dynamic.",
   "RBC believes TSLA holders would be receptive at $480 per share, which is its SOTP intrinsic value plus a roughly 15% premium. At current prices that implies an approximately 50/50 ownership split of the combined entity.",
   "SpaceX is about 70% of RBC's combined pro forma valuation. SPCX holders could contribute most of the value while owning less than half of the combined company at $480 per share, which could draw pushback.",
   "RBC sees Terafab, a joint chip manufacturing facility, as perhaps the most compelling near-term catalyst. It could remove duplicated R&D and unlock well over $1T in long-term cost savings versus sourcing chips externally, per RBC estimates.",

  "insights": [
   "Goldman Sachs estimates September core PCE inflation at 3.1% YoY, while the Dallas Fed\u2019s trimmed mean PCE measure sits at 2.2%.",
   "The gap between core and trimmed mean inflation remains elevated, largely driven by AI-related price pressures, airfare increases from energy shocks, and tariff-related goods inflation.",
   "These three factors account for approximately 75% of the current deviation of the core-trimmed mean gap from its long-run average.",
   "GS expects the impact of these three factors to diminish, as AI-related memory/computer price growth slows, tariff effects stabilize, and energy prices normalize.",
   "The firm finds little evidence of broadening inflation, noting that upper-tail trimmed categories are rotating month-to-month rather than reflecting persistent, entrenched price pressures.",
   "The trimmed mean remains a reliable guide to the underlying inflation trend, as the current skew reflects one-off shocks rather than a fundamental shift in inflation dynamics."
